q20905.en: On a one-way carriageway, the white dashed line shown marks the edges of the lanes.

explain.short: On a one-way road the dashed line in the middle shows where one lane ends and the next begins.
explain.rule: On a one-way road, the white dashed line only separates the lanes. All lanes go the same way and you may cross the line to change lane.
explain.trap: 'delimitare le corsie' (to mark the lanes) is exactly what this line does.

sceneParams.caption: One-way road: the dashed line marks the lanes

q20906.en: The white dashed line shown, on one-way roads, divides the lanes.

explain.short: The dashed line splits the one-way road into two lanes going the same way.
explain.rule: On a one-way road, the white dashed line only separates the lanes. All lanes go the same way and you may cross the line to change lane.
explain.trap: 'divide le corsie' (divides the lanes): lanes, not directions, because the road is one-way.

sceneParams.caption: Dashed line: lanes side by side, same direction

q20907.en: The white dashed line shown allows you to make a U-turn on one-way roads.

explain.short: On a one-way road you can never turn around and drive back: you would be going against the traffic. The line only lets you change lane.
explain.rule: On a one-way road, the white dashed line only separates the lanes. All lanes go the same way and you may cross the line to change lane.
explain.trap: 'inversione di marcia' (U-turn) is never allowed on a one-way road, whatever the line.

sceneParams.caption: One-way road: U-turn never allowed
lines: Dashed line: you may change lane

q20908.en: The white dashed line shown divides the road into two carriageways, each one two-way.

explain.short: A painted line does not make two carriageways; only a physical divider (spartitraffico) does. Here the line only separates lanes.
explain.rule: On a one-way road, the white dashed line only separates the lanes. All lanes go the same way and you may cross the line to change lane.
explain.trap: 'due carreggiate, ognuna a doppio senso' (two carriageways, each two-way) is invented: it is one carriageway with lanes.

sceneParams.caption: One carriageway, two lanes: not two carriageways

q20909.en: The white dashed line shown is found only on one-way roads.

explain.short: The white dashed line is used on two-way roads too, to separate the two directions. So it is not found only on one-way roads.
explain.rule: On a one-way road, the white dashed line only separates the lanes. All lanes go the same way and you may cross the line to change lane.
explain.trap: 'solo' (only) is the trap: dashed lines are on two-way roads too.

sceneParams.caption: Dashed lines: one-way AND two-way roads

q20910.en: On one-way roads, the white dashed line shown is placed on hill crests, to divide the two directions of travel.

explain.short: A one-way road has only one direction, so there are no two directions to divide. And on hill crests of two-way roads the line is solid, not dashed.
explain.rule: On a one-way road, the white dashed line only separates the lanes. All lanes go the same way and you may cross the line to change lane.
explain.trap: 'dividere i due sensi di marcia' (divide the two directions) is impossible on a 'senso unico' (one-way) road.

sceneParams.caption: One-way road: there are no two directions
lines: On crests the centre line is solid

q20911.en: The solid white centre line shown divides the carriageway into two lanes.

explain.short: The solid line in the middle splits the carriageway into two lanes, one on each side.
explain.rule: A white solid line in the middle separates the lanes, and on two-way roads it separates the two directions. You must never cross it or drive on it.
explain.trap: 'due corsie' (two lanes): one carriageway, two lanes.

sceneParams.caption: Solid centre line: two lanes

q20912.en: The solid white centre line shown must not be crossed.

explain.short: A solid line is a barrier you must respect: you may not go over it.
explain.rule: A white solid line in the middle separates the lanes, and on two-way roads it separates the two directions. You must never cross it or drive on it.
explain.trap: 'non può essere superata' (must not be crossed) is the basic meaning of a solid line.

sceneParams.caption: Solid line: do not cross
lines: Never cross it, never drive on it

q20913.en: The solid white centre line shown divides the directions of travel on two-way roads.

explain.short: On a two-way road the solid line in the middle keeps the two directions apart.
explain.rule: A white solid line in the middle separates the lanes, and on two-way roads it separates the two directions. You must never cross it or drive on it.
explain.trap: 'divide i sensi di marcia' (divides the directions): on two-way roads, yes.

sceneParams.caption: Two-way road: the line separates the directions

q20914.en: The solid white centre line shown, on two-way roads, can be found on the uphill part of a hill crest.

explain.short: Near the top of a hill you cannot see oncoming cars. A solid line stops you moving into their lane.
explain.rule: A white solid line in the middle separates the lanes, and on two-way roads it separates the two directions. You must never cross it or drive on it.
explain.trap: 'tratto in salita di un dosso' (uphill part of a crest) is a typical place for a solid line.

sceneParams.caption: Before a hill crest: solid line, no overtaking
lines: Solid line: stay in your lane

q20915.en: The solid white centre line shown, on two-way roads, can be near pedestrian crossings.

explain.short: Before a pedestrian crossing a solid line stops cars from overtaking, so people crossing are safe.
explain.rule: A white solid line in the middle separates the lanes, and on two-way roads it separates the two directions. You must never cross it or drive on it.
explain.trap: 'attraversamenti pedonali' (pedestrian crossings) are a typical place for a solid line.

sceneParams.caption: Near pedestrian crossings: solid line

q20916.en: The solid white centre line shown allows overtaking as long as you do not cross it.

explain.short: The line itself is the limit. If you can pass a slow vehicle (for example a bicycle) while staying fully in your lane, you may do it.
explain.rule: A white solid line in the middle separates the lanes, and on two-way roads it separates the two directions. You must never cross it or drive on it.
explain.trap: 'senza superarla' (without crossing it) is the key: the ban is on crossing the line, not on every overtake.

sceneParams.caption: Overtake only if you stay in your lane
lines: Pass it without touching the line

q20917.en: The solid white centre line shown divides the road into two carriageways, each one two-way.

explain.short: A painted line divides lanes, not carriageways. Two carriageways need a physical divider (spartitraffico).
explain.rule: A white solid line in the middle separates the lanes, and on two-way roads it separates the two directions. You must never cross it or drive on it.
explain.trap: 'due carreggiate, ognuna a doppio senso' (two carriageways, each two-way) is invented.

sceneParams.caption: One carriageway with two lanes, not two carriageways

q20918.en: The solid white centre line shown allows you to drive astride it.

explain.short: Driving with the line between your wheels means driving on it. A solid line must never be crossed or driven on.
explain.rule: A white solid line in the middle separates the lanes, and on two-way roads it separates the two directions. You must never cross it or drive on it.
explain.trap: 'marciarvi a cavallo' (drive astride it) is forbidden: it means you are on the line.

sceneParams.caption: Driving on the solid line: forbidden
lines: Never cross it, never drive on it

q20919.en: The solid white centre line shown allows overtaking even when crossing it, as long as only the left wheels go over.

explain.short: A solid line may not be crossed at all, not even with only two wheels.
explain.rule: A white solid line in the middle separates the lanes, and on two-way roads it separates the two directions. You must never cross it or drive on it.
explain.trap: 'purché con le sole ruote di sinistra' (as long as only the left wheels) sounds like a small exception, but there is none.

sceneParams.caption: Not even the left wheels may cross
lines: Left wheels over the line: no

q20920.en: The solid white centre line shown allows a U-turn on two-way roads.

explain.short: A U-turn would take you across the solid line. That is forbidden.
explain.rule: A white solid line in the middle separates the lanes, and on two-way roads it separates the two directions. You must never cross it or drive on it.
explain.trap: 'inversione di marcia' (U-turn) means crossing the line, which a solid line forbids.

sceneParams.caption: U-turn across a solid line: forbidden

q20921.en: The marking shown indicates the recommended speed.

explain.short: The number 50 painted on the road tells you the speed advised on that stretch.
explain.rule: A number painted on the road (iscrizione) shows the recommended speed. It is not a weight limit.
explain.trap: 'velocità consigliata' (recommended speed): a painted number is advice for your speed.

sceneParams.caption: Painted 50: recommended speed

q20921.reviewNote: Painted numbers on the road may also repeat a speed LIMIT; check that 'recommended speed' is the intended official reading.

q20927.en: Where the marking shown is present, vehicles with a laden mass over 50 quintals may not pass.

explain.short: The painted 50 is about speed, not weight. Weight limits are shown by vertical signs, not by numbers on the road.
explain.rule: A number painted on the road (iscrizione) shows the recommended speed. It is not a weight limit.
explain.trap: '50 quintali' (50 quintals, 5 tonnes) mixes up the number 50 with a weight.

sceneParams.caption: 50 on the road = speed, not weight

q20922.en: The device shown is an artificial speed hump.

explain.short: Yellow and black stripes across the road mark a raised hump that makes you slow down.
explain.rule: Yellow and black stripes across the road mark a speed hump (dosso artificiale). It makes you slow down; it is not a crossing and has nothing to do with parking.
explain.trap: 'dosso artificiale' (artificial hump) is the correct name of this device.

sceneParams.caption: Yellow-black stripes: speed hump, slow down

q20923.en: The element shown is a speed reducer installed on the road.

explain.short: A speed hump is one kind of speed reducer: it forces drivers to slow down.
explain.rule: Yellow and black stripes across the road mark a speed hump (dosso artificiale). It makes you slow down; it is not a crossing and has nothing to do with parking.
explain.trap: 'rallentatore di velocità' (speed reducer) is another name for this hump.

sceneParams.caption: Speed reducer on the road

q20924.en: The element shown represents a speed reducer.

explain.short: The yellow and black striped hump is a speed reducer: you must slow down before it.
explain.rule: Yellow and black stripes across the road mark a speed hump (dosso artificiale). It makes you slow down; it is not a crossing and has nothing to do with parking.
explain.trap: 'rallentatore di velocità' (speed reducer): yes, this is what the picture shows.

sceneParams.caption: Striped hump = speed reducer

q20928.en: The element shown is placed on a stretch of road where parking is forbidden.

explain.short: A speed hump only makes you slow down. It says nothing about parking.
explain.rule: Yellow and black stripes across the road mark a speed hump (dosso artificiale). It makes you slow down; it is not a crossing and has nothing to do with parking.
explain.trap: 'vietata la sosta' (parking forbidden) has nothing to do with a speed hump.

sceneParams.caption: Speed hump: about speed, not parking

q20929.en: The element shown marks a cycle crossing.

explain.short: A cycle crossing is marked with white squares or dashes, not with yellow and black stripes. This is a speed hump.
explain.rule: Yellow and black stripes across the road mark a speed hump (dosso artificiale). It makes you slow down; it is not a crossing and has nothing to do with parking.
explain.trap: 'attraversamento ciclabile' (cycle crossing) is a different marking.

sceneParams.caption: Not a cycle crossing: a speed hump

q20930.en: The element shown marks a pedestrian crossing.

explain.short: A pedestrian crossing has wide white stripes (zebra crossing). Yellow and black stripes mark a speed hump.
explain.rule: Yellow and black stripes across the road mark a speed hump (dosso artificiale). It makes you slow down; it is not a crossing and has nothing to do with parking.
explain.trap: 'attraversamento pedonale' (pedestrian crossing) uses white stripes, not yellow and black.

sceneParams.caption: Not a zebra crossing: a speed hump

q20925.en: The yellow boundary lines shown mark out a parking area reserved for disabled people.

explain.short: Yellow lines mark special, reserved parking places. With the yellow diagonal stripes beside the space, this is a disabled parking bay.
explain.rule: Yellow lines mark parking spaces reserved for disabled people. The yellow diagonal stripes next to the space must stay free, so the person can get in and out.
explain.trap: 'riservata a persone invalide' (reserved for disabled people) is right for this yellow bay.

sceneParams.caption: Yellow bay with stripes: disabled parking

q20926.en: The yellow diagonal stripes shown must be left free so that disabled people can get in and out of the vehicle.

explain.short: The striped area next to the bay gives space to open the door wide and use a wheelchair. Never park on it.
explain.rule: Yellow lines mark parking spaces reserved for disabled people. The yellow diagonal stripes next to the space must stay free, so the person can get in and out.
explain.trap: 'devono essere lasciate libere' (must be left free): you may not park or stop on these stripes.

sceneParams.caption: Diagonal stripes: keep free for getting in and out

q20931.en: The yellow lines shown mark out a parking area reserved for taxis.

explain.short: The diagonal stripes beside the bay show it is for disabled people, not for taxis.
explain.rule: Yellow lines mark parking spaces reserved for disabled people. The yellow diagonal stripes next to the space must stay free, so the person can get in and out.
explain.trap: 'taxi' is wrong: the striped space for getting out is the sign of a disabled bay.

sceneParams.caption: Not for taxis: for disabled people

q20932.en: The yellow lines shown mark out an area reserved for loading and unloading goods.

explain.short: The striped space for getting out of the car shows a disabled bay, not a loading area.
explain.rule: Yellow lines mark parking spaces reserved for disabled people. The yellow diagonal stripes next to the space must stay free, so the person can get in and out.
explain.trap: 'carico e scarico di merci' (loading and unloading goods) is a different reserved area.

sceneParams.caption: Not a loading bay: disabled parking

keywords.it: carico e allo scarico di merci

q20933.en: The white dashed side line shown separates the carriageway from a lay-by.

explain.short: The road widens on one side into a lay-by (piazzola di sosta). The dashed side line lets you cross into it to stop.
explain.rule: A white dashed line at the side of the carriageway marks a place where you may cross it: a lay-by, a driveway, an acceleration lane or a side road. Guide lines in a junction show your path and do not ban turns.
explain.trap: 'piazzola di sosta' (lay-by) is exactly what the picture shows.

sceneParams.caption: Dashed side line: entrance to a lay-by
lines: Dashed line: you may go in

q20934.en: The white dashed side line shown separates the carriageway from a driveway.

explain.short: The short opening on the side is a driveway (passo carrabile). The dashed line shows that vehicles may cross there to go in and out.
explain.rule: A white dashed line at the side of the carriageway marks a place where you may cross it: a lay-by, a driveway, an acceleration lane or a side road. Guide lines in a junction show your path and do not ban turns.
explain.trap: 'passo carrabile' (driveway) is the opening shown in the picture.

sceneParams.caption: Dashed side line at a driveway

q20935.en: The white dashed lines in the junction shown are guide lines.

explain.short: Inside the junction, dashed lines continue the lanes to guide your path across it.
explain.rule: A white dashed line at the side of the carriageway marks a place where you may cross it: a lay-by, a driveway, an acceleration lane or a side road. Guide lines in a junction show your path and do not ban turns.
explain.trap: 'strisce di guida' (guide lines) is the correct name for dashed lines inside a junction.

sceneParams.caption: Dashed lines in the junction: guide lines

q20942.en: The white guide lines shown do not allow turning.

explain.short: Guide lines only show the path across the junction. They are dashed, so they do not stop you turning.
explain.rule: A white dashed line at the side of the carriageway marks a place where you may cross it: a lay-by, a driveway, an acceleration lane or a side road. Guide lines in a junction show your path and do not ban turns.
explain.trap: 'non consentono la svolta' (do not allow turning) is wrong: dashed lines can be crossed.

sceneParams.caption: Guide lines are dashed: turning is allowed

q20936.en: The white dashed side line shown divides the carriageway from an acceleration lane.

explain.short: The slip road joins the main road through an acceleration lane. The dashed line lets you move from it into the main lane.
explain.rule: A white dashed line at the side of the carriageway marks a place where you may cross it: a lay-by, a driveway, an acceleration lane or a side road. Guide lines in a junction show your path and do not ban turns.
explain.trap: 'corsia di accelerazione' (acceleration lane) is the lane where joining traffic speeds up.

sceneParams.caption: Dashed side line: acceleration lane
lines: Speed up, then cross the dashed line

q20944.en: The white dashed side line shown marks out a lay-by.

explain.short: Here the lane next to the dashed line is an acceleration lane, joining from the slip road. It is not a place to stop.
explain.rule: A white dashed line at the side of the carriageway marks a place where you may cross it: a lay-by, a driveway, an acceleration lane or a side road. Guide lines in a junction show your path and do not ban turns.
explain.trap: 'piazzola di sosta' (lay-by) is wrong for this picture: it is an acceleration lane.

sceneParams.caption: Not a lay-by: an acceleration lane

q20937.en: The white dashed side line shown marks the edge of the main road, separating it from the edge of the minor road.

explain.short: Where a side road joins, the edge line of the main road becomes dashed. It shows the main road's edge and that you may cross it to turn.
explain.rule: A white dashed line at the side of the carriageway marks a place where you may cross it: a lay-by, a driveway, an acceleration lane or a side road. Guide lines in a junction show your path and do not ban turns.
explain.trap: 'strada principale' (main road): the dashed line follows the main road's edge.

sceneParams.caption: Dashed edge: main road meets side road

q20938.en: The white dashed side line shown may be crossed only in an emergency.

explain.short: A dashed line may be crossed normally. You cross it whenever you want to use the lay-by.
explain.rule: A white dashed line at the side of the carriageway marks a place where you may cross it: a lay-by, a driveway, an acceleration lane or a side road. Guide lines in a junction show your path and do not ban turns.
explain.trap: 'solo in caso di emergenza' (only in an emergency) is wrong: dashed means you may cross.

sceneParams.caption: Dashed line: cross it to use the lay-by

q20939.en: The white dashed side line shown means that stopping is not possible.

explain.short: The opposite: behind the line there is a lay-by, a place made for stopping.
explain.rule: A white dashed line at the side of the carriageway marks a place where you may cross it: a lay-by, a driveway, an acceleration lane or a side road. Guide lines in a junction show your path and do not ban turns.
explain.trap: 'la sosta non è possibile' (stopping not possible) is the opposite of what a lay-by is for.

sceneParams.caption: Lay-by: made for stopping

q20943.en: The white dashed side line shown marks the access to a cycle lane.

explain.short: The opening behind the dashed line is a driveway for vehicles, not a cycle lane.
explain.rule: A white dashed line at the side of the carriageway marks a place where you may cross it: a lay-by, a driveway, an acceleration lane or a side road. Guide lines in a junction show your path and do not ban turns.
explain.trap: 'pista ciclabile' (cycle lane) is wrong: the picture shows a driveway.

sceneParams.caption: Not a cycle lane: a driveway

q20940.en: The white dashed side line separates the carriageway from the emergency lane.

explain.short: The emergency lane is separated by a SOLID white line, because you may not enter it except in an emergency.
explain.rule: A white dashed line at the side of the carriageway marks a place where you may cross it: a lay-by, a driveway, an acceleration lane or a side road. Guide lines in a junction show your path and do not ban turns.
explain.trap: 'corsia di emergenza' (emergency lane) goes with a solid line, not a dashed one.

sceneParams.caption: Emergency lane: solid line, not dashed

q20941.en: The white dashed side line signals the start of a hard shoulder.

explain.short: The hard shoulder (banchina) is the strip beyond the solid edge line. A dashed side line marks a place you may cross into, like a lay-by or driveway.
explain.rule: A white dashed line at the side of the carriageway marks a place where you may cross it: a lay-by, a driveway, an acceleration lane or a side road. Guide lines in a junction show your path and do not ban turns.
explain.trap: 'banchina' (hard shoulder, the strip next to the carriageway) is not marked by a dashed line.

sceneParams.caption: Dashed side line: not the start of a shoulder

q20945.en: The markings shown are found near a level crossing.

explain.short: The large painted cross (X) on the road warns that a level crossing (passaggio a livello, where road and railway meet) is close.
explain.rule: Near a level crossing (passaggio a livello) the road has a painted cross and a solid centre line. Watch for trains, with or without barriers, and do not move to the left side of the road.
explain.trap: 'passaggio a livello' (level crossing) is what the painted X announces.

sceneParams.caption: Painted X: level crossing nearby
lines: Solid line: stay on the right

q20946.en: The markings shown warn drivers that they are near a level crossing without barriers.

explain.short: These markings are used before level crossings both with and without barriers. So they can warn of one without barriers.
explain.rule: Near a level crossing (passaggio a livello) the road has a painted cross and a solid centre line. Watch for trains, with or without barriers, and do not move to the left side of the road.
explain.trap: 'senza barriere' (without barriers) is fine: the markings are used for both types.

sceneParams.caption: Level crossing without barriers: yes

q20947.en: The markings shown warn drivers that they are near a level crossing with barriers.

explain.short: These markings are used before level crossings both with and without barriers. So they can warn of one with barriers.
explain.rule: Near a level crossing (passaggio a livello) the road has a painted cross and a solid centre line. Watch for trains, with or without barriers, and do not move to the left side of the road.
explain.trap: 'con barriere' (with barriers) is also fine: both types use these markings.

sceneParams.caption: Level crossing with barriers: yes

q20948.en: Where the markings shown are present, you may not move into the left part of the carriageway.

explain.short: The solid centre line before the crossing forbids moving left: no overtaking, stay in your lane.
explain.rule: Near a level crossing (passaggio a livello) the road has a painted cross and a solid centre line. Watch for trains, with or without barriers, and do not move to the left side of the road.
explain.trap: 'non è consentito spostarsi nella parte sinistra' (you may not move left): the solid line forbids it.

sceneParams.caption: Solid line: do not move to the left

q20949.en: Where the markings shown are present, drivers must watch out for trains that may be coming.

explain.short: Near a level crossing a train may arrive. Slow down, look and listen.
explain.rule: Near a level crossing (passaggio a livello) the road has a painted cross and a solid centre line. Watch for trains, with or without barriers, and do not move to the left side of the road.
explain.trap: 'eventuale sopraggiungere di treni' (trains that may be coming) is the danger of a level crossing.

sceneParams.caption: Level crossing: watch for trains

q20950.en: The markings shown indicate that there is a very dangerous tram crossing 150 metres ahead.

explain.short: The painted X warns of a level crossing with a railway, not a tram crossing. And the markings give no distance like 150 m.
explain.rule: Near a level crossing (passaggio a livello) the road has a painted cross and a solid centre line. Watch for trains, with or without barriers, and do not move to the left side of the road.
explain.trap: 'attraversamento tranviario' (tram crossing) and '150 metri' are both invented.

sceneParams.caption: Railway level crossing, not a tram crossing

q20951.en: The markings shown are found only near level crossings with barriers.

explain.short: They are used before level crossings both with and without barriers.
explain.rule: Near a level crossing (passaggio a livello) the road has a painted cross and a solid centre line. Watch for trains, with or without barriers, and do not move to the left side of the road.
explain.trap: 'solo' (only) is the trap: also without barriers.

sceneParams.caption: With AND without barriers

q20952.en: The markings shown signal that a junction controlled by the local police is near.

explain.short: The painted X warns of a level crossing, not of a junction with a police officer.
explain.rule: Near a level crossing (passaggio a livello) the road has a painted cross and a solid centre line. Watch for trains, with or without barriers, and do not move to the left side of the road.
explain.trap: 'incrocio regolato da Polizia locale' (junction controlled by police) is invented.

sceneParams.caption: Not a police junction: a level crossing

q20953.en: The markings shown mark out a parking area for public service buses.

explain.short: The painted X warns of a level crossing. A bus stop or bus area is marked differently, with yellow markings.
explain.rule: Near a level crossing (passaggio a livello) the road has a painted cross and a solid centre line. Watch for trains, with or without barriers, and do not move to the left side of the road.
explain.trap: 'parcheggio di autobus' (bus parking) is invented.

sceneParams.caption: Not a bus area: a level crossing

q20955.en: The emergency lane (lane A) may be used if the vehicle breaks down, for a maximum of three hours.

explain.short: If your car breaks down you may stop in the emergency lane, but not for more than three hours.
explain.rule: The emergency lane (corsia di emergenza) is beyond a solid white line. You may stop there only for a breakdown or an emergency, for max three hours. You may not drive or overtake in it.
explain.trap: 'per un massimo di tre ore' (for max three hours) is the time limit for a breakdown stop.

sceneParams.caption: Breakdown: stop in lane A, max 3 hours

q20956.en: The emergency lane (lane A) may not be used for overtaking.

explain.short: Lane A is beyond a solid line and only for emergencies. Overtaking in it is forbidden.
explain.rule: The emergency lane (corsia di emergenza) is beyond a solid white line. You may stop there only for a breakdown or an emergency, for max three hours. You may not drive or overtake in it.
explain.trap: 'non si può occupare per le manovre di sorpasso' (may not be used to overtake): correct.

sceneParams.caption: No overtaking in the emergency lane

q20958.en: In the markings shown, the solid white line that marks the emergency lane (lane A) indicates a time-limited parking zone.

explain.short: The solid line marks the emergency lane, which is for emergencies only. It is not a parking area of any kind.
explain.rule: The emergency lane (corsia di emergenza) is beyond a solid white line. You may stop there only for a breakdown or an emergency, for max three hours. You may not drive or overtake in it.
explain.trap: 'zona di parcheggio a tempo' (time-limited parking) is invented; time-limited parking has blue lines.

sceneParams.caption: Emergency lane, not timed parking

q20959.en: In the markings shown, the solid white line that marks the emergency lane (lane A) may always be crossed when traffic is heavy.

explain.short: Heavy traffic is not an emergency. You may not cross the solid line to drive in the emergency lane.
explain.rule: The emergency lane (corsia di emergenza) is beyond a solid white line. You may stop there only for a breakdown or an emergency, for max three hours. You may not drive or overtake in it.
explain.trap: 'sempre' (always) and 'intenso traffico' (heavy traffic): a queue is no reason to use lane A.

sceneParams.caption: Heavy traffic: stay out of lane A
lines: Queue in lanes B and C

q20960.en: The emergency lane (lane A) is reserved for turning right.

explain.short: Lane A is for emergencies and breakdowns, not for turning.
explain.rule: The emergency lane (corsia di emergenza) is beyond a solid white line. You may stop there only for a breakdown or an emergency, for max three hours. You may not drive or overtake in it.
explain.trap: 'svolta a destra' (right turn) is invented for this lane.

sceneParams.caption: Lane A: emergencies, not right turns

q20961.en: The emergency lane (lane A) is reserved for slowing down.

explain.short: Slowing down to exit is done in a deceleration lane, which has a dashed line. Lane A is for emergencies only.
explain.rule: The emergency lane (corsia di emergenza) is beyond a solid white line. You may stop there only for a breakdown or an emergency, for max three hours. You may not drive or overtake in it.
explain.trap: 'decelerazione' (slowing down) belongs to the deceleration lane, not the emergency lane.

sceneParams.caption: Lane A is not a deceleration lane

q20962.en: The emergency lane (lane A) is closed to cars but not to motorcycles.

explain.short: Driving in the emergency lane is forbidden for all vehicles, motorcycles included.
explain.rule: The emergency lane (corsia di emergenza) is beyond a solid white line. You may stop there only for a breakdown or an emergency, for max three hours. You may not drive or overtake in it.
explain.trap: 'ma non al transito dei motocicli' (but not to motorcycles) is an invented exception.

sceneParams.caption: Lane A: forbidden for cars AND motorcycles

q20963.en: The solid transverse line shown indicates the point where you must stop at a junction, if it is controlled by a red traffic light.

explain.short: At a red light you stop before the solid line across the lane.
explain.rule: The solid white line across the lane (stop line) shows where you must stop when you have to: red light, a police officer's order, or a STOP sign.
explain.trap: 'semaforo a luce rossa' (red traffic light): this is a case when you must stop at the line.

sceneParams.caption: Red light: stop before the line

q20964.en: The solid transverse line shown indicates the point where we must always stop at a junction, if the traffic officer orders it.

explain.short: When a traffic officer tells you to stop, you stop at the stop line.
explain.rule: The solid white line across the lane (stop line) shows where you must stop when you have to: red light, a police officer's order, or a STOP sign.
explain.trap: 'sempre ... se il vigile lo impone' (always, if the officer orders it): 'always' is right because of the condition.

sceneParams.caption: Officer says stop: stop at the line

q20965.en: The solid transverse line shown indicates the point where you have to stop.

explain.short: With the word STOP painted before it, this line is where you must stop before entering the junction.
explain.rule: The solid white line across the lane (stop line) shows where you must stop when you have to: red light, a police officer's order, or a STOP sign.
explain.trap: 'arrestarsi' (to stop): with a STOP, you must always stop at the line.

sceneParams.caption: STOP + solid line: always stop here

q20966.en: The solid transverse line shown indicates the point where we must stop at a junction, if it is not controlled.

explain.short: At this junction the line is for stopping at a red light or on an officer's order. 'Not controlled' is the opposite of the case shown.
explain.rule: The solid white line across the lane (stop line) shows where you must stop when you have to: red light, a police officer's order, or a STOP sign.
explain.trap: 'se non è regolato' (if not controlled) is wrong: you stop here when the junction IS controlled.

sceneParams.caption: Stop line: for controlled junctions
lines: Stop line: red light or officer

q20967.en: The solid transverse line shown indicates the point where you must always stop near a road junction.

explain.short: You stop at this line only when you must: red light or officer. With a green light you go on.
explain.rule: The solid white line across the lane (stop line) shows where you must stop when you have to: red light, a police officer's order, or a STOP sign.
explain.trap: 'sempre' (always) is the trap: not always, only when required.

sceneParams.caption: Not always: only on red or on order
lines: Red light: stop at the line

q20968.en: The solid transverse line shown indicates that you must give way to vehicles coming from both the right and the left.

explain.short: The line only shows WHERE to stop. It does not by itself create a give-way rule; here the junction is controlled.
explain.rule: The solid white line across the lane (stop line) shows where you must stop when you have to: red light, a police officer's order, or a STOP sign.
explain.trap: 'obbligatorio dare la precedenza' (must give way): the line marks a stopping point, not a give-way order.

sceneParams.caption: Stop line: where to stop, not a give-way rule
lines: It is not a give-way order

q20969.en: The solid transverse line shown is found at the exit of a private property.

explain.short: The picture shows a junction between public roads. This line is a stop line at a junction, not the exit of a private property.
explain.rule: The solid white line across the lane (stop line) shows where you must stop when you have to: red light, a police officer's order, or a STOP sign.
explain.trap: 'proprietà privata' (private property) is not what the picture shows.

sceneParams.caption: Stop line at a junction, not a private exit
lines: Stop here when you must stop
